3.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
3.text: "It's been a while, Mr. Rayne. Let me catch you up on my activities since I left office."

10.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
10.text: "Before we move on, I want to talk about the elephant in the room. The events that preceded the '53 election."
10.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Diplomatic"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_CampaignedForAlphonso"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Backstab"] == true)

14.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
14.text: “President Rayne, I am here because we have a great opportunity on our hands. A business arrangement that will benefit Gasom and Sordland alike.”
14.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Diplomatic"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_CampaignedForAlphonso"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Backstab"] == true) == false)

15.speaker: Gus Manger
15.text: “And serve you did. Sordland would be much worse off without you.”

16.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
16.text: "I put so many years of my life into this corporation. And then I left it all behind and devoted myself to serving the people of Sordland."

17.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
17.text: “The structure was rotting from the inside. It needed a shake-up.”

18.speaker: Player
18.text: "Yes, you helped rescue the country from Soll's extreme protectionist and isolationist policies."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: "Gasom continues to thrive, doesn't it? Your tenure as president may have come to an end, but it's not as if you were left with nothing."

23.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
23.text: "I never would have imagined you capable of such a betrayal. Especially after you provided such invaluable support during my party leadership contest against Soll."

24.speaker: Gus Manger
24.text: “There might have been some disagreements in the past, but the President has shown strong leadership and good decision-making.”
24.conditionsRaw:
Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn01_PersonalInvestment_DontSpend"] == false  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_PromoteMarket"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_Diplomacy_West"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_Immigration_Relaxed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Intention"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or 
Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true)

25.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
25.text: "I never would have imagined you capable of such a betrayal.”

26.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
26.text: “I also happen to believe that current and former presidents of Sordland should stick together and share our experiences. Not everyone has been in our shoes, you know."

27.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
27.text: "These two pillars embody the lasting impact we leave behind and the way we are remembered by others."

28.speaker: Narrator
28.text: He gazed out for a moment longer as he contemplated what I'd said, then turned back to us.

32.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
32.text: “My Gasom is not nearly as bad off as the Sordish government was. But a shake-up is needed nonetheless.”

33.speaker: Gus Manger
33.text: “The latest figures show that Gasom will have to either decrease staff and operations by 40 percent in one year or take on a crushing amount of debt.”

34.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
34.text: “I appreciate you coming through, Gus. Getting Rizia interested in another investment is a major feat.”

35.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
35.text: “But I'm concerned about the future of what I have built up."

36.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
36.text: "But let's shift our focus to Gasom."

37.speaker: Gus Manger
37.text: “This is why we have decided to reach out to foreign investors."

38.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
38.text: “We've got an amazing opportunity here. The demand for gas is steadily increasing from both international partners and the Sordish state. All we have to do is ensure a consistent supply."

39.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
39.text: "I've had some time to think since leaving office. And to me, all of life's complexities can be distilled into two elements. Reputation and legacy."

40.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
40.text: “With the right amount of investment, we can expand resource extraction, effectively fulfill rising demand and ensure long-term stability and profitability.”

41.speaker: Player
41.text: "I cannot help but empathize with individuals who invest their utmost dedication and passion into their work."

42.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
42.text: “Not the right choice of words. This is not a bailout, but a strategic long-term cooperation.”

43.speaker: Player
43.text: “The fact that a leading privatizer is coming to the state to bail out his corporation is hysterical.”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “You do know that Rizia can't invest more than 20 percent unless the government permits the transaction which can take a long time.”

45.speaker: Player
45.text: “Gasom is a private corporation. What does Sordland have to do with your business?”

46.speaker: Player
46.text: “If your analysis is correct, any investment would also make returns and secure further gas.”

47.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
47.text: “I ventured to Xina, immersing myself in its vibrant culture, then traversed the captivating landscapes of the Anrakan archipelago, and finally reunited with old acquaintances in Kyow.”

48.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
48.text: “And now that you're in office, you seem to be turning your back on your ideals entirely. Is power getting to you?”
48.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_WarnTraitors"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Intention"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true

49.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
49.text: “I always spoke highly of you, in fact. The youngest MP, a prodigy, I said. Even though I knew we could be rivals one day.”

50.speaker: Player
50.text: "It's too early to tell whether the Alphonso era was good for Sordland. It'll be a subject of debate among future historians."

51.speaker: Player
51.text: "The deviation from our planned economic strategy didn't bode well for the nation."

52.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
52.text: "Gasom still operates, yes. 'Thrives' is perhaps an exaggeration."

53.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
53.text: "That is much appreciated. I am well aware of the challenges you yourself have faced. I commend you for navigating those obstacles without causing harm to others."

54.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
54.text: "That's why Mr. Manger and I have been diligently exploring alternative solutions."

55.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
55.text: "If Soll had continued, we would have faced a severe economic downturn as well. The fabric of the country was being torn apart by corruption, greed and autocratic tendencies."

56.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
56.text: "We're not here to talk about my presidential successes or failures, Mr. Rayne. But I will say this."

57.speaker: Narrator
57.text: The sound of sirens briefly distracted us. Through the window, we saw police cars driving down the street adjacent to the Gasom zone.

58.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
58.text: “I will remind you that I was never against the complete removal of the Energy Protection Act of 1932.”

65.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
65.text: “In fact, I saw eye to eye with Soll about protecting our natural resources from foreign interests. But there is a balance in all things.”

67.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
67.text: "I hope you won't stand idly by once again while the country is in desperate need of economic support."

68.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
68.text: "Your government has recently provided stimulus payouts to Sordish citizens, so you understand the necessity of such investments."

69.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
69.text: “Which is precisely why you were invited to be a part of this discussion.”

70.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
70.text: "Considering your own recent bailouts of businesses, you're hardly in a position to judge."

71.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
71.text: “We provide gas to half of Sordland, Mr. President. We could earn even more by selling gas abroad, but we value national advantage.”

72.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
72.text: "Why settle for being in the top 10 energy exporters when we have the potential to compete with Arcasia and United Contana?"

73.speaker: Gus Manger
73.text: “Mr. President, Gasom is a strategic asset to this nation regardless of its ownership."

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “We don't need another nation to take care of our own energy company. Couldn't we keep this between Sordland and Gasom?”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: "Considering the current state of the government budget, it may not be prudent to allocate additional funds."

76.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
76.text: "The right economic decisions can increase those funds. Gasom is poised for significant growth."

77.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
77.text: "To be honest, I prefer engaging with you and the Sordish government over foreign powers who prioritize their own interests."

78.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
78.text: "Indeed. This deal has the potential to bolster both Gasom and Sordland. Together, we can create a historic opportunity."

79.speaker: Gus Manger
79.text: “The reality of Arcasian-style capitalism means that our national interests should absolutely be part of the discussion.”

81.speaker: Player
81.text: “Investing together with Rizia could be better than just letting them purchase as much as they can.”

82.speaker: Gus Manger
82.text: “It might seem risky. But if we lose this opportunity, we might never have the chance again.”

86.speaker: Player
86.text: “Don't act so innocent. You and I both know how this game is played."

87.speaker: Player
87.text: “Blind? No, I see the truth all too well."

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “The nation needs strong leadership after our fall from grace.”

91.speaker: Player
91.text: “Why didn't you approach the large international banks in Kyrute or Anraka? They might be eager.”

92.speaker: Gus Manger
92.text: "Mr. Alphonso has neglected to mention that this is not an either/or proposition. Sordland can invest alongside Rizia."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "We've got the budget for it. And such a cooperation could be beneficial."

97.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
97.text: “Very beneficial. I will be at the helm to ensure these funds bring sustainable growth and good returns.”

99.speaker: Gus Manger
99.text: “Ewald won't be alone. We have a talented financial team.”

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “I did what I had to do. Just like you did to beat Soll in the '46 Congress. Don't act like we are different.”

101.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
101.text: “Did the road to power blind you?”
101.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_WarnTraitors"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Intention"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true) == false

102.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
102.text: “If we are going to work together, we'd better figure out if we are on the same page.”

103.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
103.text: “As presidents of this republic there is more that binds us than that separates us. I want to establish a good partnership.”

104.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
104.text: “And you are providing it? Have you looked outside the palace windows?”

105.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
105.text: “This isn't a game. If something fruitful is to come out of our talk today, we need to establish trust.”

106.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
106.text: “We worked well together before, and we can again. But our intentions must be genuine.”

107.speaker: Player
107.text: “And I appreciate your kind words but I want to iterate that the past is in the past. No reason to be petty.”

108.speaker: Player
108.text: “Your term may have come to a rough end. This doesn't mean I don't respect you.”

109.speaker: Player
109.text: “I worked with you because I believed in your vision. But opinions change, and so do allegiances.”

110.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
110.text: “I think there is a strong potential for a deep partnership. The government strengthens the security of gas and the company can compete and grow.”

111.speaker: Gus Manger
111.text: “And after we draw other investors, the state can always sell shares for a higher price and make a return.”

112.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
112.text: “It would be more costly from the government perspective, but a worthwhile endeavor.”

116.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
116.conditionsRaw:
Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn01_PersonalInvestment_DontSpend"] == false  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_PromoteMarket"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_Diplomacy_West"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_Immigration_Relaxed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Intention"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or

Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true)) == false

118.speaker: Narrator
118.conditionsRaw:
(Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn01_PersonalInvestment_DontSpend"] == false  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_PromoteMarket"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn01_InT_Investment_Railway"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_Diplomacy_West"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Promise_Immigration_Relaxed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Intention"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or 
Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true)) == false

119.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
119.text: “Until '51, that is. Then the Sollist deep state began their damaging acts against our democracy.”

120.speaker: Gus Manger
120.text: “Gentleman, I think we are losing sight of our goal.”

123.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
123.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_WarnTraitors"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Intention"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true

124.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
124.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_StatusReaction_WarnTraitors"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Intention"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true) == false

125.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
125.text: “I beat that contest fairly. The era of Soll was ending. All I provided was a future vision.”

126.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
126.text: “And Tarquin Soll didn't obstruct me initially. He actually respected the will of the party and gave me free reign.”

127.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
127.text: “And I guess you can empathize as to where my lack of optimism comes from."

128.speaker: Player
128.text: "Optimism is a choice, Ewald. And sometimes, it's a difficult one to make."

129.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
129.text: “The future of this corporation matters as much to me as it does to the nation of Sordland.”

131.speaker: Player
131.text: "Yes, Ewald, we've seen division. Now it's a question of how we overcome it."

132.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
132.text: “Why travel far for what you can achieve at home, or with our good friends in Rizia?"

133.speaker: Gus Manger
133.text: “Some international banks are interested, but they would rather buy the entirety of Gasom. Which is not possible, at least for now.”

134.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
134.text: “Co-investing would reduce Sordland's contribution while allowing the nation to still have a stake for strategic purposes.”

135.speaker: Gus Manger
135.text: “If the treasury situation is a concern, this path could be the most optimal.”

136.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
136.text: “I have been in your shoes. I saw the country descend into infighting, first in the Maroon Palace and then on the street."

137.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
137.text: “I'm an optimist, you know. I came here today despite everything because I believe we can still find common ground."

138.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
138.text: “You know what they say. Fool me once...”

141.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
141.text: "I trust you comprehend Sordland's need for energy independence, President Rayne, especially as we labor to recover from the recession."

142.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
142.text: “Indeed. I've always considered you a strategic ally, President Rayne.”

143.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
143.text: “Don't you see the mutual benefit in our collaboration?”

144.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
144.text: "Of course, we've had our differences. But the people have chosen you. The nation's future is in your hands."

146.speaker: Player
146.text: “We were always meant to work together.”

147.speaker: Player
147.text: “You are the reason that I am where I am now.”

148.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
148.text: “Despite our past differences, our visions for Sordland still intersect.”

152.speaker: Gus Manger
152.text: “Other nations also heavily weighed against Sordland in that period.”

153.speaker: Player
153.text: “I know there were other factors, Ewald. But you have to admit you played a part in your own downfall.”

154.speaker: Player
154.text: “It's easy to blame everyone else for your own faults, isn't it?"

155.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
155.text: “You should thank the obstructionists of the Old Guard and their disagreements with Soll for that.”

156.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
156.text: "That's easier said than done, isn't it?"

157.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
157.text: "But without optimism, what do we have? Despair? That's no way to lead."

158.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
158.text: "Something like that. My point is, it would be unwise to attempt another double-cross."

159.speaker: Gus Manger
159.text: "It's a tough road, sure. But we can't just roll over. Sordland needs us, gentlemen."

160.speaker: Gus Manger
160.text: "We can't afford despair either, can we? Let's keep our heads up and our eyes forward."

161.speaker: Gus Manger
161.text: "Let's not let old grudges cloud our judgment, gentlemen."

162.speaker: Player
162.text: "Division is a fact of life, Ewald. The challenge is how we navigate it."

163.speaker: Player
163.text: "Sometimes countries need to go through social division to change."

164.speaker: Player
164.text: "Optimism, Ewald? That's a luxury I can't afford."

165.speaker: Player
165.text: "I am as optimistic as you are, Ewald. We cannot afford to lose hope."

166.speaker: Player
166.text: "I wouldn't come all this way just to fool you, Ewald."

167.speaker: Player
167.text: "I have a country to lead. Why should I even bother speaking to you?"

168.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
168.text: "A difficult choice, but often the only one that can propel us forward."

169.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
169.text: "Indeed, President Rayne. And it seems our methods of navigation might differ."

170.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
170.text: "But how many people will suffer because of that division?"

174.speaker: Player
174.text: "Let's put the past aside, Ewald. I have a country to run."

175.speaker: Player
175.text: "This is indeed a business arrangement, Ewald. Let's focus on that."

176.speaker: Player
176.text: "Presidents sticking together? That's an interesting notion."

177.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
177.text: "Of course, President Rayne. Business, above all, should drive this discussion."

178.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
178.text: "Indeed, it is an interesting notion, President Rayne. It's a shame that politics often stand in the way."

179.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
179.text: "A sentiment I share, President Rayne. The welfare of Sordland must always be our top priority."

180.speaker: Gus Manger
180.text: "Exactly, gentlemen! Let's get down to brass tacks, eh?"

181.speaker: Gus Manger
181.text: "Could do with a bit more of that, couldn't we? Former presidents, current presidents, all pulling together for Sordland!"

182.speaker: Gus Manger
182.text: "That's the spirit, gentlemen! Sordland is above most else, am I right?"

183.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
183.text: "As we discuss the future of Sordland, it is paramount that I comprehend your vision."

184.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
184.text: "Now I hear that you are positive about the Kingdom of Rizia investing in Gasom."

185.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
185.text: "On the other hand, I have not heard any indication of your leanings regarding the Kingdom of Rizia's interest in investing in Gasom."

187.speaker: Player
187.text: "My greatest concern is for the well-being of Sordland, whether that involves a collaboration with Rizia or not."

188.speaker: Player
188.text: "Yes, I take it as an encouraging sign that a foreign nation is interested in a Sordish corporation."

189.speaker: Player
189.text: "I am certainly receptive to the idea, but engaging with international partners like monarchies brings its own set of bad repercussions."

190.speaker: Player
190.text: "While the prospect of collaborating with a wealthy nation like Rizia is not unappealing, I am suspicious of their underlying intentions."

191.speaker: Player
191.text: "I have yet to receive a comprehensive briefing on the matter. I prefer to maintain a careful approach, and not make premature commitments."

192.speaker: Player
192.text: "I'd rather not hand over crucial components of our energy industry to foreign entities."

193.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
193.text: "The trajectory you set for this country will inevitably impact not just Gasom, but also Sordland's position on the global stage."

194.speaker: Player
194.text: "Look, I am open to make sense out of why I have come all the way here."

195.speaker: Player
195.text: "I understand your perspective, and it is justified to a degree. I want to explore an earnest way out."

196.speaker: Player
196.text: "I do understand your perspective, but I'm not here to care about your problems."

197.speaker: Player
197.text: "For the future of Sordland, it is the best interest of all if Gasom remains in Sordish hands."

198.speaker: Player
198.text: "We have state energy corporations that can do what you are doing with Gasom. Better, even."

199.speaker: Player
199.text: "Gasom plays a crucial role in Sordland's energy independence. It must be controlled."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "That just shows how weak our so-called 'democracy' is."

201.speaker: Player
201.text: "The reforms while bold were conducted way too quick. If they had succeeded any deep state attempt would have failed."

202.speaker: Player
202.text: "I've come face to face with the Old Guard myself now. I understand what you were up against."

203.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
203.text: “I believe they can be defeated. But not without allies.”

204.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
204.text: "Our democracy is not weak. It has been tested, but it has also shown resilience. We should not confuse struggle with weakness."

205.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
205.text: "You're quick to judge from the comfort of hindsight. We acted decisively, yes, but that's what was needed at the time."

206.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
206.text: "The state's interest and Gasom's success are not mutually exclusive. Our control can be shared."

207.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
207.text: "I can't disagree. But it's not about who owns Gasom, it's about how it's run."

208.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
208.text: "Then by all means, let them try. Competition is the lifeblood of progress. Let the best corporation win."

209.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
209.text: "These aren't just my problems. They're Sordland's problems. And if you're not here to care about them, then why are you here?"

210.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
210.text: "Well, isn't that magnanimous of you. It's not about making sense of why you're here. It's about understanding the critical role you play in shaping the future of Sordland."

211.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
211.text: "Then let's do that. For Sordland's sake, we need to find common ground."

212.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
212.text: "You make a valid point, President Rayne. The interest of foreign investors could indeed be seen as an endorsement of our potential for growth and competitiveness."

213.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
213.text: "Your caution is well-founded, President Rayne. International partnerships are fraught with complexity."

214.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
214.text: "Indeed, Mr. President. The welfare and progress of Sordland must always be our primary concern."

215.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
215.text: "I respect your prudence, but let us not forget that fortune often favors the bold."

216.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
216.text: "It's encouraging to hear your concern for Sordland's key industries, Mr. President."

217.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
217.text: "Your wariness is understandable, President Rayne. The motivations of nations like Rizia are not always clear-cut."

218.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
218.text: "However, I would caution that such interest is not a guarantee of our success."

219.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
219.text: "However, I trust that you recognize the potential opportunities and benefits they might bring to Sordland."

220.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
220.text: "Maintaining control of these sectors is indeed crucial, but we must also consider the potential benefits that foreign investment might bring."

221.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
221.text: "Our utmost priority should be to ensure that any partnership we enter is in the best interest of Sordland."

222.speaker: Player
222.text: "You're correct, Gus. We need to refocus. Ewald, let's set our differences aside and aim for the best possible outcome for Sordland."

223.speaker: Player
223.text: I don't know. If our visions for Sordland are fundamentally at odds, is there even a point to continue this discussion?"

225.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
225.text: "Our reputation, what we're known for during our time, can shape our legacy, what we leave behind. The two are inseparable."

226.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
226.text: "We should strive to build a reputation that speaks to our values and a legacy that demonstrates our impact on Sordland."

227.speaker: Gus Manger
227.text: "Right you are, Ewald. How can a man be judged, if not by the impact he makes on others and the way he is remembered?"

228.speaker: Player
228.text: "I agree. Our reputation is the mirror of our actions, and our legacy, the shadow that remains."

229.speaker: Player
229.text: "An interesting take. But reputation is transient, while legacy is lasting. The latter is what truly matters."

230.speaker: Player
230.text: "A valid point, Mr. Alphonso. But I would argue that integrity and service to the people should stand above reputation and legacy."

231.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
231.text: "Very well, President Rayne. Our personal differences shouldn't overshadow the future of our country and my company."

232.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
232.text: "Your words hint at resignation, President Rayne. But I still believe in the possibility of a consensus, despite our differences."

233.speaker: Gus Manger
233.text: "I'm glad to see you both finding common ground. Let's proceed with Sordland's interests at heart."

234.speaker: Player
234.text: "I believe we've exhausted the possibilities here, Ewald. Our visions for Sordland are just too divergent."

235.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
235.text: "That's unfortunate, President Rayne. I was hoping we could find some middle ground. But I respect your stance."

236.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
236.text: "Good. Because you're on my territory right now, and another double-cross would be a terrible mistake."

237.speaker: Gus Manger
237.text: "Gentlemen, let's remember that we're here to make a new agreement, not rehash old disagreements."

238.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
238.text: "I'm well aware of the responsibilities of leadership, President Rayne. Have you never thought that you could benefit from my experience?"

239.speaker: Gus Manger
239.text: "Mr. President, Ewald, let's not lose sight of the fact that we all want what's best for Sordland. We may have different ideas, but our goals are the same."

246.speaker: Player
246.text: "You're right, Ewald. Our country needs both energy independence and economic recovery. Perhaps a collaboration could be beneficial."

247.speaker: Player
247.text: "Our goals may align, Ewald, but that doesn't mean we need each other. Sordland isn't your responsibility anymore."

248.speaker: Player
248.text: "I'm not convinced, Ewald. Your past actions make me skeptical of your intentions."

249.speaker: Player
249.text: "Your vision for Sordland has its merits, Ewald. However, my administration has its own path to tread."

250.speaker: Player
250.text: "Our visions heavily intersect, Ewald. We should try our best to work together."

251.speaker: Player
251.text: "Common visions are not always grounds for alliances, Ewald."

252.speaker: Player
252.text: "The people's favor is a heavy burden, Ewald. One I intend to bear with honor and integrity, unlike you."

253.speaker: Player
253.text: "It's not about favor, Ewald. It's about making the right decisions for our country."

254.speaker: Player
254.text: "The people's favor is transient, Ewald. What matters is the legacy we leave behind."

255.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
255.text: "That's the spirit, President Rayne. Together, we can accomplish great things."

256.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
256.text: "True. It's yours. But remember, no man is an island."

257.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
257.text: "I understand your skepticism. But we can't let past misunderstandings get in the way of a fruitful future."

258.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
258.text: "Yes, every administration has its own path. But don't disregard the wisdom of those who have trod it before you."

259.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
259.text: "Indeed, President Rayne. I will respect your autonomy in decision-making."

260.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
260.text: "True, President Rayne. But sometimes, unexpected alliances can bring about the greatest changes."

261.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
261.text: "Your bitterness casts doubts that you will, President Rayne. It is not wise to make enemies for no reason."

262.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
262.text: "Indeed, President Rayne. The right decisions, however, aren't always the easiest ones."

264.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
264.text: "Have I told you about I became involved with Gasom?"

265.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
265.text: "It was all because I seized an opportunity. I bought the shares being sold by the Contanan partners and secured a significant stake. This move wasn't just about financial gain or personal ambition."

266.speaker: Narrator
266.text: We redirected our attention to the meeting.

267.speaker: Narrator
267.text: Alphonso took a sip of coffee before continuing.

268.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
268.text: "After acquiring the shares, I was elected as CEO. The company expanded, hired world-class engineers from all over the world, turned the small town of Narbel into a thriving city."

269.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
269.text: "Despite criticism from the Nature Preservation Foundation, I fulfilled most of the gas needs of Sordland and increased our energy independence, all while aligning with Tarquin Soll's autarky strategy."

270.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
270.text: "That's the essence of opportunity. What matters is that you seize it when it appears. And remember, it's not just about taking that leap, but about what you do once you've landed."

271.speaker: Narrator
271.text: He took a sip of coffee. His face assumed a contemplative expression.

272.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
272.text: "I see them as more than just reflections and shadows. They are the tangible products of our actions, the fruits of our labor."

273.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
273.text: "I would argue that the transient nature of reputation is what makes it important. It's the soil in which the seed of legacy grows."

274.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
274.text: "A noble perspective. But isn't it through our reputation and legacy that our integrity and service are ultimately judged?"

275.speaker: Player
275.text: "Your past actions show nothing but a ruthless pursuit of profit, at the expense of the people and environment. That's hardly a reputation or a legacy to be proud of."

276.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
276.text: "A harsh critique, but not an unexpected one. I see profit as a means to a greater end. It enables us to drive progress, change lives."

277.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
277.text: "As for my legacy, it will be for history to judge, not you or me."

278.speaker: Gus Manger
278.text: "It seems we are at a crossroads with Gasom. The numbers tell a tale of struggle and potential."

279.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
279.text: "No need to sugarcoat it, Gus. Our corporation is teetering on the edge of a cliff. Without significant restructuring, the firm risks plunging into insurmountable debt."

280.speaker: Gus Manger
280.text: "My old friend Ewald reached out to me for assistance. Out of respect for our shared history -- and my small stake in the company -- I couldn't refuse."

281.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
281.text: "Thanks to Gus' Rizian connections, investors from the kingdom are now interested in Gasom, a development that could steer us clear of the looming crisis."

282.speaker: Player
282.text: "I'm intrigued by the untapped fields. What's the potential return if we invest in these new areas?"

283.speaker: Player
283.text: "Will the investment help keep Gasom from having to downsize its operations?"

284.speaker: Player
284.text: "That's a risk, Mr. Alphonso. What if the investment doesn't pay off as expected?"

285.speaker: Gus Manger
285.text: "It was only when his father fell ill that he took over and transformed the farm. He took risks, made some mistakes, but ultimately, he tripled their output in just a few years."

286.speaker: Gus Manger
286.text: “Your concerns, Mr. President, remind me of a time when I was working with OMEC. We were bringing in foreign investments to revitalize the local companies. There were protests, people who were scared of change, who thought we were selling out. But we weathered the backlash, stood by our decisions.”

287.speaker: Player
287.text: "A heartwarming story, Gus. But one successful case doesn't necessarily mean it's the best approach for the whole country."

288.speaker: Player
288.text: "A truly inspiring story, Gus. This is the kind of innovation and growth we should be fostering in Sordland."

289.speaker: Player
289.text: "Wait a minute, Gus. Is this story about you? Were you the young farmer?"

290.speaker: Gus Manger
290.text: “Years later, those same people saw the benefits, the jobs we created, the growth we spurred. Change is always met with resistance, but in the end, it's the results that matter.”

291.speaker: Player
291.text: "That's a nice story, Gus, but we're not talking about a company here, we're talking about an entire nation. The stakes are much higher."

292.speaker: Player
292.text: "Your experience with OMEC is very valuable for us, Gus. We do need to stay the course and see our decisions through."

293.speaker: Player
293.text: "Change may be met with resistance, Gus, but it's our job to ensure that the people are with us on this journey. We can't disregard their concerns."

294.speaker: Gus Manger
294.text: "Ha! Well, I did grow up on a farm, but no, that wasn't me. I was too busy trying to turn apples into a viable fuel source. A failed experiment, but it made some damn good cider!"

295.speaker: Gus Manger
295.text: "That's the power of economic freedom. It allows innovation, it allows us to adapt and to grow."

296.speaker: Gus Manger
296.text: "Of course not, Mr. President. But if we completely turn our backs on the idea of economic freedom, we're no worse than that farmer's father."

297.speaker: Gus Manger
297.text: "I completely agree, Mr. President. The people are our greatest asset."

298.speaker: Gus Manger
298.text: "It's true, OMEC was a great learning experience."

300.speaker: Gus Manger
300.text: "But remember, sometimes, people don't know what's best for them until they see it. That's why we're here, to help them see a better future."

301.speaker: Gus Manger
301.text: "A lot of sleepless nights, tough negotiations, and even a few broken friendships... but I'd do it all over again if it means seeing our country prosper."

302.speaker: Gus Manger
302.text: "But remember, a nation is also a conglomerate of sorts, of people, of businesses, of hopes and dreams."

303.speaker: Narrator
303.text: As Gus finished his point, we suddenly heard the faint wailing of sirens in the distance. He waited for the noise to fade before continuing.

304.speaker: Player
304.text: "I don't like bullshit. Just tell me what you want from me."

305.speaker: Player
305.text: "I will at least hear the details of your proposal. But I won't make any promises."

307.speaker: Player
307.text: "You talk about seizing opportunities, yet your rapid privatization nearly crashed our economy. That's rich, considering your 'leap' resulted in anything but a graceful landing."

308.speaker: Player
308.text: "Your approach might have worked for you, but it's not always as simple as that."

311.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
311.text: "But that requires us to be willing to take risks and weather the storm. Now, that's a legacy worth striving for, wouldn't you agree?"

312.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
312.text: "Every investment involves risk. But this one is an easy bet."

313.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
313.text: "That's the question of the hour, Mr. President. It won't be easy, but with the right moves, we might be able to navigate this storm without losing our crew."

315.speaker: Gus Manger
315.text: "I've always believed in the power of networking. I'm sure you've heard of Rusty Montoro, Chairman and CEO of Rizian Royal Gold. Rusty and I go way back, and he's done quite well for himself."

316.speaker: Gus Manger
316.text: "Back under Alphonso's government, I was able to broker a deal with King Romus Toras, thanks to my connection with Rusty. It was a win for all involved."

317.speaker: Player
317.text: "Rusty Montoro, the Toras family, the Rizian government...it seems like an impressively powerful alliance you've formed."

318.speaker: Player
318.text: "So I've heard, Gus. I understand the need for strategic alliances, but let's remember our own interests and values."

319.speaker: Player
319.text: "With all due respect, Gus, I'm not thrilled that you got Sordland in bed with a monarchy. The kingdom's connection to Rumburg isn't particularly reassuring either."

320.speaker: Gus Manger
320.text: "It was quite a feat, and not one without risk. But the potential rewards for Sordland, I believe, are worth it."

321.speaker: Gus Manger
321.text: "I hear your concern, but business doesn't always line up neatly with politics. Our deal with the Toras family was purely about economic growth for Sordland."

322.speaker: Gus Manger
322.text: "Absolutely, we're in this for Sordland first and foremost. But remember, in the world of international business, alliances are tools, not ties that bind us."

326.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
326.text: "Our pace was not the problem. Resistance to change was."

327.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
327.text: “Along the way, I had the privilege of encountering remarkable individuals who have made significant contributions to their respective fields.”

328.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
328.text: "My experiences prompted deep reflection on the essence of life. I came out of it all with two words resonating in my head: reputation and legacy."

329.speaker: Narrator
329.text: With a cup of coffee in hand, he strolled over to the window, his gaze drawn to the expansive gas fields stretching before him. Towering mountains provided a majestic backdrop.

330.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
330.text: "I have been thinking about my own legacy and reputation. And I refuse to be remembered as a failed reformer."

331.speaker: Player
331.text: "Don't we all yearn to be remembered and to make a meaningful contribution?"

332.speaker: Player
332.text: "Life's true essence lies in the present moment."

333.speaker: Player
333.text: "The focus on reputation and legacy is rooted in a capitalist framework that perpetuates individualism and inequality."

337.speaker: Narrator
337.text: After taking a moment to appreciate the landscape, Alphonso turned back to us.

339.speaker: Player
339.text: "That makes sense. Foreign investors will bring much-needed capital and expertise."

340.speaker: Player
340.text: "Engaging with foreign investors can be a double-edged sword."

341.speaker: Player
341.text: "I have concerns about relying too heavily on foreign investors. It's important to prioritize local ownership and maintain sovereignty over our national resources."

343.speaker: Gus Manger
343.text: "I understand your concerns. But the future of Gasom is on the line."

344.speaker: Gus Manger
344.text: "I appreciate your perspective, but we need to adapt to the changing global landscape."

348.speaker: Player
348.text: "Foreign investors such as the Kingdom of Rizia, you mean?"

349.speaker: Gus Manger
349.text: "The Kingdom of Rizia certainly has valuable expertise and resources in the energy sector."

352.speaker: Gus Manger
352.text: "It's a strategic move to ensure the growth and success of Gasom, benefiting both the company and the nation."

353.speaker: Gus Manger
353.text: "Rest assured, we will take measures to protect our interests and ensure responsible engagement."

354.speaker: Gus Manger
354.text: "Foreign investors will bring new opportunities and technologies that could enhance the efficiency and competitiveness of Gasom. It's about finding the right balance and safeguarding our interests."

355.speaker: Gus Manger
355.text: "We will carefully consider their investment proposal and assess how it aligns with our long-term goals for Gasom."

356.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
356.text: “The trouble is that right now, some of our fields are operating at only half of their capacity due to resource limitations. But we have significant potential for expansion, including two new fields that haven't even been tapped."

362.speaker: Player
362.text: “I won't let the Old Guard do what they did to you to me. You should have seen through it.”

363.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
363.text: "You'll need allies if you want to beat the deep state, Mr. Rayne. A difficult proposition for a traitor."

364.speaker: Player
364.text: "I don't like bullshit. Can we get to the choice at hand?"

366.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
366.text: "One would expect more diplomatic skill from a president."

367.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
367.text: "Your lack of statesmanship is disheartening, President Rayne."

369.speaker: Player
369.text: "I've seen enough corporate bailouts and handouts to know that it's always the big businesses that benefit, while the common people are left to suffer."

370.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
370.text: "Gasom is not just another corporation; it's an essential part of the energy infrastructure that powers our nation."

372.speaker: Gus Manger
372.text: "With proper investment and development, we project extremely high returns in the first five years alone."

373.speaker: Gus Manger
373.text: "We have developed a strategic plan that focuses on diversifying revenue streams and exploring new markets."

374.speaker: Gus Manger
374.text: "There is the aforementioned interest from Rizia. But the investment could also come from Sordland itself."

375.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
375.text: "As chair, my own reputation and legacy are tied with that of Gasom. But so, I would argue, are Sordland's."

376.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
376.text: "I confess I've been following the news from the Maroon Palace closely since leaving office."

387.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
387.text: "I am heartened that your economic interests seem to align with mine."
387.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_PromoteMarket"] == true)

388.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
388.text: "Your decision to deviate from a market economy is, let's say, not what I would have chosen."
388.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn02_EconomicRelief_BailedBusinesses"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_PromoteMarket"] == true) == false)

395.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
395.text: "Even more so that you have chosen to align with the West. It's a path I myself considered while drafting my foreign policy."

396.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
396.text: "But I am heartened by your decision to align with the West. It's a path I myself considered while drafting my foreign policy."

399.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
399.text: "But I am puzzled that your administration has so far ignored the wealth of opportunities provided by the West. It's not a foreign policy direction I would have chosen."

401.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
401.text: "And I am puzzled that your administration has so far ignored the wealth of opportunities provided by the West."

406.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
406.text: "Meanwhile, I have not heard any indication of your leanings regarding the Kingdom of Rizia's interest in investing in Gasom."

407.speaker: Gus Manger
407.text: "You know, gentlemen, this reminds me of a story from when I was just starting out."

408.speaker: Gus Manger
408.text: "There was this young farmer in Gruni. His father was a stubborn man, insisted on doing things the old way. But this young farmer, he had ideas. He wanted to modernize, to innovate."

410.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
410.text: “We've got an amazing opportunity here. The demand for gas is steadily increasing from both international partners and the Sordish state. All we have to do is ensure a consistent supply."

411.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
411.text: “With the right amount of investment, we can expand resource extraction, effectively fulfill rising demand and ensure long-term stability and profitability.”

412.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
412.text: “The trouble is that right now, some of our fields are operating at only half of their capacity due to resource limitations. But we have significant potential for expansion, including two new fields that haven't even been tapped."

419.speaker: Player
419.text: "I can assist you if you can return the favor by improving the situation in the city."

421.speaker: Player
421.text: "I will seize opportunities, but not the ones you might like."

422.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
422.text: "I respect a man that sticks to his ideals."

423.speaker: Player
423.text: "Our image and our perception are a key force that shape our lives. But they can also be burdensome."
